Title: A prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial about safety and efficacy of combined treatment with alteplase (rt-PA) and Cerebrolysin in acute ischaemic hemispheric stroke
Author: Lang W, Stadler CH, Poljakovic Z, Fleet D, and the Lyse Study Group
Comment: The paper reports no risk ratio, odds ratio or p-value for mortality; only raw counts (4 vs 4) are given. Safety population equals the ITT/randomised population (60 vs 59), so randomised group sizes were used as denominators.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Alteplase (rt-PA) + Cerebrolysin 30 ml/day i.v. for 10 days') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Country: Austria, Croatia and other European centres (14 hospitals in 5 countries)
Participant type: adults aged 18-80 with acute ischaemic hemispheric stroke treated with rt-PA within 3 h of onset
Recruitment source: 14 hospitals in five countries, February 2005 - March 2008
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died out of number randomised per arm (safety/ITT population)

Report_ID: All-cause mortality (death before day 30; longest mortality reporting available)
Title: Cerebrolysin effects on neurological outcomes and cerebral blood flow in acute ischemic stroke
Author: Amiri-Nikpour et al.
Comment: No formal significance test (no P-value, RR or OR) reported for mortality; only raw counts and percentages. Mortality reported only up to day 30 even though follow-up was 90 days. Randomised Ns (23/23) used as denominators since deaths were excluded from the analysed Ns (22/21).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Cerebrolysin 30 mL IV daily for 10 days + aspirin 100 mg') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adults aged 18–85 years with acute focal ischemic stroke (NIHSS 6–22) admitted 6–24 hours after onset
Recruitment source: Imam Khomeini Hospital, Urmia University of Medical Sciences, Urmia, Iran (March 2013–March 2014)
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died out of the number randomised in each arm
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality (death before day 30; longest mortality reporting available)
effect_direction: favours Cerebrolysin (1/23 vs 2/23; RR ~0.50), not significant

Report_ID: All-cause mortality (deaths during the study, day 90 / end of trial)
Title: Neuroprotective treatment with Cerebrolysin in patients with acute stroke: a randomised controlled trial
Author: Ladurner, Kalvach, Moessler, and the Cerebrolysin Study Group
Comment: No formal significance test of the mortality difference is reported; only event counts and percentages. Table 2 shows "All SAEs (deaths)" as 6 (6) Cerebrolysin vs 7 (6) placebo, consistent with 6 deaths per arm. Randomised group sizes (78/68) used as denominators per plan.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Cerebrolysin 50 mL/day IV for 21 days + ASA + pentoxifylline') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults aged 45-85 with first acute ischaemic stroke in the middle cerebral artery territory, treated within 24 h of onset
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died out of the number randomised in each arm
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality (deaths during the study, day 90 / end of trial)

Title: Cerebrolysin in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke in Asia: Results of a Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Randomized Trial (CASTA)
Author: Heiss et al.
Comment: Denominators are the treated/safety population (529 Cerebrolysin, 540 placebo); randomised Ns were 529 and 541 (1 untreated patient excluded). The reported hazard ratio of 1.26 is oriented so that values >1 favour Cerebrolysin (inverse of the usual treatment-vs-control HR direction), so it was NOT entered into the hazard_ratio field to avoid a direction error. Overall cumulative placebo mortality stated as 6.6% in the mortality section vs 5.9% in the safety section; event counts are consistent.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Cerebrolysin 30 mL/day IV x10 days + aspirin 100 mg') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Country: China, Hong Kong, South Korea, Myanmar
Participant type: adults (18-85 y) with acute hemispheric ischemic stroke, NIHSS 6-22, treated within 12 h
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died out of patients treated/randomised per arm
effect_direction: favours Cerebrolysin, not significant (28/529 vs 32/540; RR ~0.89, P=0.19)
